# Results — Study 440 (Floor-Trader Pivot Points)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **price
respects the floor-trader pivots (P, R1–R3, S1–S3) as intraday support/resistance** — tested as
a touch→bounce study on **5-minute** bars, pinned against the only honest baseline: a horizontal
line placed at a **random** price on the same tape. A "touch" is a bar straddling the level
within 5 bps; a "bounce" is price moving away from the level (up off support, down off
resistance) over the next 6 bars (30 min), entered one bar after the touch (no look-ahead).
Offline & deterministic once the 5-minute cache exists; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance **5-minute** OHLC bars (`auto_adjust=False`), 5 liquid names: SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, IWM |
| Window | **2026-03-30 → 2026-06-23** (~12 weeks; **59 full sessions per name**) |
| As-of | **2026-06-24** (pull date; the live 2026-06-24 partial session is dropped — no partial sessions in a stamped run) |
| Fingerprints (close) | SPY `ba71a0483420` · QQQ `9f0cf1426369` · AAPL `3d7a6f9e0b7d` · MSFT `bdcbbb4d34bf` · IWM `6c652b12c810` |
| Levels | classic floor-trader `P = (H+L+C)/3` from the **prior** session; `R1=2P−L, S1=2P−H, R2=P+(H−L), S2=P−(H−L), R3=H+2(P−L), S3=L−2(H−P)` |
| Touch / bounce / costs | touch within **5 bps**; bounce over **k = 6 bars (30 min)**, entered **1 bar after** the touch; fade cost **1 bp** one-way (2 bp round trip) |

> **Short-span & capacity caveat (named on the Signal axis).** Yahoo caps 5-minute history at
> ~60 calendar days, so this is ~12 weeks on 5 surviving liquid names — enough power to reject a
> *tradable* effect (and to show pivots don't beat random lines), **not** enough to certify a
> tiny one. Intraday fades are round-tripped in minutes, so the **bid-ask spread** is the binding
> constraint; we charge a deliberately generous 2-bp round trip for these ultra-liquid names.

## The signal — pivots vs randomly-placed control lines (pooled across the basket)

| line | touches | bounce rate | mean fade | HAC *t* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **floor-trader pivots** | 1,410 | **0.467** | **−1.12 bps** | **−1.04** | 46.7% |
| randomly-placed control | 5,782 | 0.501 | +0.36 bps | +0.82 | — |

The pivots bounce **46.7%** of the time — *below* both a coin flip and the random-line control
(**50.1%**), a **−3.4-point deficit**. The fade trade earns **−1.12 bps** per touch at **HAC
*t* = −1.04** (gross, already on the wrong side of zero). The floor-trader arithmetic is not a
better support/resistance map than a line drawn at random.

## Bounce rate by pivot level (deep support → far resistance)

| level | n touches | bounce rate | mean fade |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| S3 | 102 | 0.637 | +9.06 bps |
| S2 | 190 | 0.516 | +1.61 bps |
| S1 | 373 | 0.496 | +0.35 bps |
| R1 | 445 | 0.425 | −3.15 bps |
| R2 | 221 | 0.412 | −5.05 bps |
| R3 | 79 | 0.392 | −5.37 bps |

The only level above 50% is **S3** (63.7%) — but on just **102** touches in a basket that drifted
up after deep-support touches, i.e. *the tape rose*, not *the line held*. Every resistance
(R1/R2/R3) bounces **below** a coin flip. No level reliably does its advertised job.

## Per-name — the gap is negative on 4 of 5 names

| ticker | pivot rate | control rate | diff | mean fade | HAC *t* | net fade | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 0.465 | 0.505 | −0.040 | −0.66 bps | −0.53 | −2.66 bps | 0.985 |
| QQQ | 0.429 | 0.497 | −0.068 | −1.31 bps | −0.65 | −3.31 bps | 1.000 |
| AAPL | 0.439 | 0.497 | −0.058 | −4.69 bps | −1.93 | −6.69 bps | 1.000 |
| MSFT | 0.539 | 0.519 | +0.020 | +0.97 bps | +0.31 | −1.03 bps | 0.005 |
| IWM | 0.460 | 0.490 | −0.030 | −0.07 bps | −0.03 | −2.07 bps | 0.985 |

Only MSFT shows a marginally positive pivot-minus-control gap (+0.020, placebo *p* = 0.005) — and
even there the fade is **negative net** (−1.03 bps) at HAC *t* = +0.31. One name out of five
brushing significance, in the *opposite* direction to the other four, is the texture of noise.

## Costs — the fade is negative before costs

| | fade return per touch |
|---|--:|
| gross | **−1.12 bps** |
| net of 2-bp round trip | **−3.12 bps** |

There is no cost sweep to run: the **gross** edge is already below zero, so every realistic spread
only deepens the loss. Capacity and market impact are moot — there is no edge to scale.

## Permutation placebo — a random line is at least as good as the pivots

Re-drawing the random control lines **300** times across the basket, the control bounce rate is
**0.498 ± 0.0075**, and

> **p(control rate ≥ pivot rate 0.467) = 1.00.**

Essentially *every* random line matches or beats the pivots. This is the cleanest possible NONE:
not merely indistinguishable from random — slightly **worse** than random.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic 5-minute tape where we **plant** a genuine bounce away from the pivots, the
touch→bounce test behaves exactly as it must:

| planted edge | touches | pivot rate | control rate | mean fade | HAC *t* | win-rate | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.0** (null) | 227 | 0.489 | 0.505 | −0.17 bps | −0.06 | 48.9% | 0.813 |
| **1.5** (planted bounce) | 196 | 0.704 | 0.530 | +32.90 bps | **+7.79** | 70.4% | 0.000 |

With **no** planted bounce the synthetic pivots match the control (HAC *t* = −0.06 — noise cannot
fake it); a planted bounce lights up at **t = 7.79**, placebo *p* = 0. The measurement is
unbiased — so the real-tape **t = −1.04** at a bounce rate *below* random is a genuine null, not a
blind test.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The pivot touch→bounce rate (**0.467**) is *below* both the random-line
  control (**0.501**) and a coin flip; the fade trade is **−1.12 bps** at **HAC t = −1.04**; the
  permutation placebo gives **p = 1.00** (a random line is at least as good as the pivots). The
  synthetic control proves the harness detects a planted bounce at **t = 7.79**, so this is a true
  null. (Short-span / 5-name survivorship caveat on this axis — enough to reject a tradable
  effect, not to certify a tiny one.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The fade is **−1.12 bps**/touch gross and **−3.12 bps** net of a 2-bp
  round trip. Negative before costs — nothing to size, nothing to scale.
- **"Price respects the level"? — BUSTED.** An arbitrary horizontal line bounces *more often*
  than the floor-trader pivots. The pivot arithmetic carries no support/resistance information
  beyond a line drawn at random.
